name: @kitora/overlay
description: Kitora's overlay stack: a headless core, React bindings, styled presets, a router adapter and an imperative API.

exports.name: CLOSE_REASONS
exports.description: Every reason an entry can close: a dismissal, or `resolved` (the overlay produced its value).

exports.name: DISMISS_REASONS
exports.description:
Why an entry closed without a value. `parent` and `replaced` come from the
stack itself, `back`/`route` from the router adapter, the rest from Base UI's
`onOpenChange` reasons mapped by the binding. Kept separate from
`CLOSE_REASONS` so `OverlayResult`'s dismissed branch is a real tuple type,
not an `Exclude` nobody can iterate.

exports.name: isPolicyReason
exports.description: True for the reasons a `DismissPolicy` gates. A type guard so callers narrow to `PolicyReason`.

exports.name: OVERLAY_DRIVERS
exports.description: How an entry was opened. All three drivers open and close the same entries.

exports.name: OVERLAY_KINDS
exports.description:
Behaviour and a11y role. Kind and surface are independent: an `alertdialog`
may render as a bottom sheet, a `dialog` centred or fullscreen. Menus and
tooltips are not kinds: Base UI owns them.

exports.name: OVERLAY_LAYERS
exports.description:
Paint-order bands, bottom first, named not numbered; the theme maps
each to a CSS variable. `windows` holds floating-window desktops
(`@kitora/windows`): it sits below `overlay`, so a menu
or dialog opened from inside a window paints above every window. The order of
windows inside the band is the windows kit's, not this stack's.

exports.name: OVERLAY_STATUSES
OVERLAY_SURFACES
exports.description: Presentation. The core never reads it; it is vocabulary for the bindings and presets.

exports.name: POLICY_REASONS
exports.description:
The user gestures a `DismissPolicy` can switch off. They are also the only
reasons that act on the TOP entry alone: an Escape, outside press, swipe or
Back belongs to whatever the user sees in front, never to an entry behind it.

exports.name: CloseReason
exports.description: Why an entry closed, a dismissal or `resolved`: one of `CLOSE_REASONS`.

exports.name: DismissReason
exports.description: Why an entry closed without a value: one of `DISMISS_REASONS`.

exports.name: OverlayDriver
exports.description: Which driver opened an entry (JSX, an imperative call or a route): one of `OVERLAY_DRIVERS`.

exports.name: OverlayKind
exports.description: An overlay's behaviour and a11y role: one of `OVERLAY_KINDS`.

exports.name: OverlayLayer
exports.description: A paint-order band an overlay renders in: one of `OVERLAY_LAYERS`.

exports.name: OverlayStatus
exports.description: An entry's lifecycle state: one of `OVERLAY_STATUSES`.

exports.name: OverlaySurface
exports.description: How an overlay is presented on screen: one of `OVERLAY_SURFACES`.

exports.name: PolicyReason
exports.description: A user gesture a `DismissPolicy` can switch off: one of `POLICY_REASONS`.

exports.name: counterIds
exports.description: The default factory: a per-stack counter, so two stacks on one page never share ids by accident of order.

exports.name: OverlayId
exports.description: The id of one overlay entry. Unique per stack; never reused after the entry closes.

exports.name: OverlayIdFactory
exports.description: Mints ids for one stack. Injectable (`StackOptions.createId`) so SSR and tests can make them deterministic.

exports.name: dismissedResult
exports.description: Builds the dismissed branch.

exports.name: isResolved
exports.description: Narrows to the resolved branch.
exports.signature: <R>(result: OverlayResult<R>) => result is { readonly status: "resolved"; readonly value: R; }

exports.name: resolvedResult
exports.description: Builds the resolved branch.

exports.name: resultValue
exports.description:
The `.value()` sugar as a plain function: the value when resolved, else
`undefined`. Callers that need the dismiss reason use the result itself;
callers whose `R` itself admits `undefined` should too, since the sugar
cannot tell "resolved with undefined" from "dismissed".

exports.name: OverlayResult
exports.description: The settled outcome of one entry. Settles exactly once, when the close is decided.

exports.name: BACK_FIRST
exports.description:
`escape: "back-first"`: while the body's view stack (`useOverlayNav`) can go
back, Escape pops one view and the entry stays open; at the first view it
closes as usual (O9). With no view stack registered it behaves like `true`.

exports.name: DEFAULT_DISMISS
exports.description:
Defaults per kind.
- `dialog`: every gesture except Back (Back for non-route overlays is opt-in).
- `alertdialog`: no outside press: a blocking decision is never made by a stray click.
- `popover`: like dialog; light dismiss is what a popover is.
- `panel`: Escape only (the binding routes Escape to a non-modal panel only while focus is inside it).

exports.name: DEFAULT_MODAL
exports.description: Dialogs block the page; popovers and panels do not.

exports.name: RESOLVE_ON_OUTSIDE
exports.description:
`outside: "resolve"` turns an outside press (or focus leaving an anchored
entry) into the entry's own decision instead of a dismissal: the stack calls
the commit the body registered (`useOutsideCommit`), which usually resolves
with the draft, so "click away saves" (O12). Guards are not asked, because
resolving is the overlay's decision; busy still refuses it. An entry with
this policy and no commit registered fails loudly rather than guessing.

exports.name: resolveDismissPolicy
exports.description:
The kind's defaults with a caller's partial override on top. Key by key with
`??` rather than a spread, so an explicit `{ escape: undefined }` (common when
a preset forwards an optional prop) keeps the default instead of erasing it.

exports.name: WHEN_PRISTINE
exports.description:
`outside: "when-pristine"` lets an outside press close the entry only while
no guard reports dirty; when dirty the press is ignored (no confirm), which is
the right default for forms. `outside: true` on a dirty entry routes
through the guard instead (dirty → confirm).

exports.name: DismissPolicy
exports.description:
One switch per gesture. Keys are exactly `PolicyReason` (adding a gesture
breaks this type); `outside` and `escape` also take the modes above.

exports.name: ModalMode
exports.description:
`modal: true` = inert outside + focus trap + scroll lock; `"trap-focus"` = focus
trap only (the page stays scrollable and visible to AT); `false` = neither.

exports.name: isConfirmVerdict
exports.description: Narrows a verdict to the confirm branch.
exports.signature: (verdict: GuardVerdict) => verdict is { readonly confirm: ConfirmSpec; }

exports.name: CloseAttempt
exports.description: One close attempt as a guard sees it. Never `resolved`: resolving is the overlay's own decision.

exports.name: CloseGuard
exports.description: Veto/confirm hook an entry registers for non-resolve closes; the stack asks it only while `dirty()` is true.

exports.name: ConfirmSpec
exports.description:
Copy for the nested confirm a guard asks for. Every field is optional: the
binding fills gaps from the `overlay.*` message catalog, so the core
never ships English.

exports.name: GuardConfirmer
exports.description: The binding's confirm renderer. The core cannot draw UI, so it asks through this one seam.

exports.name: GuardConfirmRequest
exports.description:
What the stack hands the binding when a guard asked for a confirm. The
binding opens its confirm UI as a child of `id` (so Escape on the confirm
closes the confirm, not the guarded entry) and answers true for "discard".

exports.name: GuardVerdict
exports.description: A guard's answer: let it close, refuse, or ask the user (allow on yes).

exports.name: walkOpenerChain
exports.description:
The return-focus walk: the first available own candidate; else the parent
overlay's content while the parent is still open (focus must stay inside a
parent that traps it); else the parent's own chain; else `fallback` (the
binding passes `body`). Returns null only when nothing at all is available.
exports.signature: (ref: OpenerRef | null, parentContent: ParentContentLookup, fallback: FocusTarget | null) => FocusTarget | null

exports.name: FocusTarget
exports.description: Somewhere focus can return to. The DOM layer wraps an element; tests and other renderers use plain objects.

exports.name: OpenerRef
exports.description:
Where focus goes when an entry closes, recorded at open time. `candidates`
are in preference order (e.g. the menu item, then the menu's trigger). The
parent link is a SNAPSHOT of the parent's own chain, so the walk still works
after the parent entry has been removed from the stack.

exports.name: ParentContentLookup
exports.description: What the walk needs to know about live parents: their content target while they are still open.

exports.name: createOverlayStack
exports.description: Creates one stack. One per `OverlayProvider`; tests create their own.

exports.name: EntrySpec
exports.description: What a driver passes to open one entry. Everything but `kind` has a documented default.

exports.name: OverlayEntry
exports.description: One entry as the outside world sees it: an immutable snapshot, replaced when anything on it changes.

exports.name: OverlayStack
exports.description: The framework-free overlay stack: the single owner of open order, parentage, close reasons and return focus.

exports.name: OverlayTicket
exports.description:
The opener's grip on one entry. Resolution with a value lives HERE, not on
the stack by id: only the code that opened the entry knows `R`, so this is
the one place a value can be type-checked against the result type.

exports.name: StackOptions
exports.description: Construction options for `createOverlayStack`; every field optional so the core has no DOM or UI dependency.

exports.name: keyboardLayerSource
exports.description: A keyboard `LayerSource` over `stack`: the top active entry is the layer on top.

exports.name: KeyboardLayerSource
exports.description: Structurally the keyboard kit's `LayerSource`.

exports.name: useEnclosingOverlayId
exports.description: The id of the overlay this component renders inside (the default parent of what it opens), or null on the page.

exports.name: useGuardConfirmView
exports.description: The provider's confirm view (the styled one under `OverlayUiProvider`), so `confirm()` and the guard confirm look the same.

exports.name: useOptionalOverlayRuntime
exports.description:
The enclosing provider's runtime, or null when no `OverlayProvider` is above.
Never throws, unlike every other hook here: a kit (form, datagrid) asks it
to decide whether to mount its own provider (standalone, tests, third-party
hosts) or to join the app's shared stack. See `EnsureOverlayUi`.

exports.name: useOverlayHost
exports.description: Where an overlay opened from here renders: the nearest `OverlayScope`'s host, else the provider's root host.

exports.name: useOverlayMessages
exports.description: The provider's resolved `overlay.*` catalog: what layers above read their default copy from.

exports.name: useOverlayRuntime
exports.description: The runtime (stack + root host) of the enclosing `OverlayProvider`.

exports.name: OverlayRuntime
exports.description: A stack plus its root host registry: everything a provider needs that is not React.

exports.description: Turns the spec a guard returned into view props, filling each missing field from the message catalog; `destructive` falls back to true.

exports.name: dirtyGuard
exports.description:
The common guard: dirty while `isDirty()` says so, and then asks the user
(copy from `spec`, gaps from the `overlay.*` catalog) before any close.

exports.name: useCloseGuard
exports.description:
Registers `guard` on the nearest overlay while mounted. Pass a new
object every render freely: the latest one is read at check time, and the
registration only changes when the guard switches between set and null.

exports.name: useOutsideCommit
exports.description:
What an outside press does on an entry opened with `dismiss={{ outside:
"resolve" }}` (O12): usually `() => ctl.resolve(draft)`, so clicking away
saves. The latest function is called; registered while mounted.

exports.name: useOverlay
exports.description:
The controller of the nearest enclosing overlay. `R` is declared by the
caller, like any context value; it must match the opener's result type
(`<Overlay onResult>` / `useOverlayScope().open<R>`). Throws outside an overlay.

exports.name: useOverlayEntries
exports.description: Every entry in the provider's stack, in paint order (devtools, a "n open" badge, tests).

exports.name: ControllerCloseReason
exports.description: The reasons body code may close with; gestures come from the renderer, structural reasons from the stack.

exports.name: OverlayController
exports.description: What an overlay body gets from `useOverlay<R>()`: its status, busy/error state and the ways to finish.

exports.name: rethrowAsync
exports.description:
Where a rejected close goes when nobody awaits it (a renderer's dismiss, a
Close button). The stack rejects only on a configuration error (a guard threw,
a confirm was asked with no confirmer), so it must surface as an uncaught
error rather than be swallowed. `reportError` is not in every environment
(jsdom lacks it), so rethrow from a microtask, which every runtime reports.

exports.name: activeElementTarget
exports.description: The element focused right now (the implicit opener when no trigger is known), or null on the server or when nothing is focused.

exports.name: BODY_FOCUS_TARGET
exports.description: A walk's last stop. Resolved lazily so a stack created during SSR never touches `document`.

exports.name: elementTarget
exports.description:
Wraps one element as somewhere focus can go. Unavailable once it left the document (row deleted, menu
unmounted), is disabled or sits under `inert`, so a walk over several candidates moves on to the next.

exports.name: createOverlayHandle
exports.description:
Creates a handle; create it at module or component scope and pass it to both the triggers and the overlay. The state is
`@kitora/primitives`' popup handle store (the one implementation every popup handle shares: popover, dialog, menu and the
rest); this adapts it to the overlay's own `open(payload, opener)` / `getSnapshot` shape.

exports.name: OverlayHandle
exports.description: A detached open/close switch with a typed payload, shared by many triggers and one `<Overlay handle>`.

exports.name: OverlayHandleState
exports.description: What a handle holds right now. `payload` survives `close()` so the exit animation still renders the closing content.

props.description: Whether the handle's overlay is open.

props.name: opener

close but the popover still stops the keydown's propagation.

exports.name: MaskedNavigator
exports.description:
Performs a masked navigation (O23) to `href` with the router's `navigate`.
Built by `maskedOverlay`, where the app's typed mask target is known, so the
adapter itself never names a route.

exports.name: OverlayNavigation
exports.description: How a route overlay navigation lands in history.

exports.name: anyDirty
exports.description: True while any active entry reports dirty: the page should ask before unloading.

exports.name: NAVIGATION_ACTIONS
exports.description: The router's history actions (TanStack's `HistoryAction`, restated so this file imports no router).

exports.name: navigationBlocked
exports.description:
True = block the navigation. Order:
1. Back with a target (a sentinel entry, or the route overlay the URL loses):
   Back belongs to the entry in FRONT (`POLICY_REASONS` act on the top only),
   so when something is stacked above the target the front entry is asked
   with `back` and the history stays put; otherwise the target closes with
   `back` and its guards may veto.
2. Everything else the navigation removes closes with `route`, top first,
   each through its guards; the first refusal blocks.
exports.signature: (stack: OverlayStack, intent: NavigationIntent, rules: NavigationRules) => Promise<boolean>

exports.name: NavigationAction
exports.description: One of the router's history actions: one of `NAVIGATION_ACTIONS`.

exports.name: NavigationIntent
exports.description: A navigation described for the overlay stack: what it does to history, the path and the route overlays.

exports.name: NavigationRules
exports.description: How navigations treat the overlays the stack holds.

exports.name: maskedOverlay

O23: the overlay whose canonical home is a page (photo, record). A soft open
from the list navigates with a TanStack route mask — the address bar shows

over it; a hard load of that URL renders the page route, which renders the
same body as a page. Pass `unmaskOnReload: true` in the mask to make a
reload a hard load too (TanStack's default keeps the overlay on reload).

(def: RouteOverlayDef

, mask: (params: P) => ToMaskOptions) => RouteOverlayDef
